evidence: This is a framing/premise statement ('heterogeneous stages deserve separately provisioned pools'), not an isolated data claim, and it is accurately labeled as the thesis's premise. The premise is discharged by the thesis body: the trace-eda decorrelation (images/s CV^2=3.83, ACF half-life 69min, Hurst ~0.93, vs requests/s CV^2=0.32, half-life 9min) and the fleet-sizing facts in baselines (encoder demand swings 2->8 workers across windows independently of the language pool's TP shape) show the stages have divergent, independently-varying demand that a single shared pool provisioning cannot track. The normative 'deserve' is warranted by that evidenced heterogeneity.
fix: None needed; the causal link (stage heterogeneity -> separate provisioning) is supported by the thesis's own characterization.
